messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Local Level Model Issue
parts:
The compiler warnings can be ignored safely. The domain_errors mean
the sampler tried a parameter value which resulted in a bad value
somewhere along the line. This is normal, particularly in the
adaptation stage.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Local Level Model Issue
parts:
The issue is that the model

------------
data {
int[0,] J; // number of days
real y[J]; // Polls
}
parameters {
real alpha[J];
real[0,.1] tau;
}
model {
alpha[1]~uniform(0,1);
for(i in 2:J)
alpha[i]~normal(alpha[i-1],tau);
for(i in 1:J)
y[i]~normal(alpha[i],0.01);
}
---------------

tries to sample

alpha[1] ~ uniform(0,1);

but doesn't constrain alpha[1] to fall between 0 and 1.

So what happens is that in initialization or when
randomizing momentum in each iteration, alpha[1] is going
outside its support in the 0 to 1 range, and thus
uniform() returns not-a-number (NaN).

Fix 1.
Put a different prior on alpha[1].

For instance,

alpha[1] ~ normal(0,100);

If you just drop the sampling statement for
alpha[1], you implicitly have an improper uniform
prior on alpha[1]. Because alpha[1] is constrained
through the sampling statement for alpha[2] in the
loop, this might work. In general, the posterior
must be proper.

Fix 2.
Define alpha[1] separately with a constraint.

real<lower=0,upper=1> alpha_1;

and then make alpha one element shorter:

real alpha[J-1];

and then you can sample

alpha_1 ~ uniform(0,1);

We've changed the constraint syntax on you since
your first post. This is probably the last syntax change
before the 1.0 release, and we'll try very hard to
maintain backward compatibility after that.

Then you'll need to change the rest of the model:

for(i in 2:J)
alpha[i]~normal(alpha[i-1],tau);
for(i in 1:J)
y[i]~normal(alpha[i],0.01);

to something where the new indexing is one less

alpha[1] ~ normal(alpha_1,tau);
for (i in 2:(J-1))
alpha[i] ~ normal(alpha[i-1],tau);

y[1] ~ normal(alpha_1,0.01);
for (i in 2:J)
y[i] ~ normal(alpha[i-1],0.01);

This kind of loop unfolding and consequent index
fiddling's a pain, but we don't have a way to
define a constraint on a single member of
an array.

An only slight less efficient alternative would be to
define a derived

real<lower=0,upper=1> alpha_1
real alpha_raw[J-1];

and then a transformed parameter

transformed parameters {
real alpha[J];
alpha[1] <- alpha_1;
for (j in 2:J)
alpha[j] <- alpha_raw[j-1];
}

Then you can use alpha as before.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: Local Level Model Issue
parts:
Thank you for the quick response! I ended up just restricting the entire vector to [0,1] since I'm working with proportions anyway. 

I'm having issues using the mean function. The root issue seems to be when I define fixed effects in the model block:

for(i in 1:NORG) 
house[i]~normal(0,HouseSigma);

and then try to normalize them in the transformed parameter block before the model uses them:

for (j in 1:NORG)
house2[j]<-house[j]-housemean;

and then the model uses them as 


##Measurement Model 
for(i in 1:NPOLLS)   
y[i]~normal(alpha[i]+house2[org[i]]+alpha[date[i]]    ,
sqrt(alpha[date[i]]*(1-alpha[date[i]])/SampleSize[i])*PIE1)
;
. 

The model runs fine if I don't normalize the fixed effects, but when I try it with them, the model returns pretty lengthy error output and doesn't generate any iterations. This sort of code works on BUGS, does the mean function cause problems when used this way in STAN?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: bounds and += operator error in mean calculation
parts: On 8/23/12 1:43 PM, dynotec wrote:> Thank you for the quick response! I ended up just restricting the entire vector to

[0,1] since I'm working with
> proportions anyway.

Well that's the right thing to do, then. It'll
keep all the values restricted to [0,1].

You might want to switch to our newer syntax, which
will go out in version 1.0. It uses named arguments
for the bounds, but is otherwise the same.

> I'm having issues using the mean function. ....

Thanks for the report. Your model should work as
written. I'll fix it and push a patch.

The key line in the error output is the following, which
says we're missing an operator+=() specialization or
have called something wrong:

...
include//stansrc/stan/math/matrix.hpp:731: error: no match for ‘operator+=’

in ‘sum += ((const std::vector<stan::agrad::var, std::allocator<stan::agrad::var> >*)v)
->std::vector<_Tp, _Alloc>::operator[]
[with _Tp = stan::agrad::var, _Alloc = std::allocator<stan::agrad::var>](i)’

- Bob
